parsed.why: Decriminalised; courts recognise trans identity; no documented trans violence or police targeting. But no gender-identity protections, no administrative recognition, societal discrimination and mixed officials keep it below Reduced Risk.

Same-sex legal, but trans discrimination is documented in healthcare, employment and schools; no gender-identity protections or LGBTI registration; toilet backlash. No criminalisation or documented police violence.

Same-sex offences remain and are used as a police lever; documented extortion, 69 violence cases against trans women and courtroom exclusion; cross-dressing ban struck down and acceptance rising, but no hate-crime recourse.

No same-sex ban but no protections; morals-law prosecution, police/army torture, militia targeting with impunity and censorship; state violence and collapsed authority dominate, despite lack of explicit criminalisation.

National gender-identity and hate-crime protections, provincial recourse and identity-based custody; rising hate crime, survey violence and anti-trans rollbacks in some provinces reduce but do not erase high safety.
